title: Question 1.7
statement_text: For fixed $k \geq 4$, is there a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a $k$-connected graph $G$ with maximal local connectivity $k$, finds a $k$-colouring of $G$, or determines that none exists?
context_text: The local connectivity $\kappa(x,y)$ of distinct vertices $x,y$ is the maximum number of internally vertex-disjoint $x$–$y$ paths, and the local edge-connectivity $\lambda(x,y)$ the maximum number of edge-disjoint $x$–$y$ paths. A graph has maximal local connectivity $k$ if $\kappa(x,y)\le k$ for all distinct $x,y$, and maximal local edge-connectivity $k$ if $\lambda(x,y)\le k$ for all distinct $x,y$; the first class contains the second, which contains all graphs of maximum degree $k$. By a theorem of Mader, all these graphs are $(k+1)$-colourable. For a $k$-connected graph with maximal local connectivity $k$, $\kappa(x,y)=k$ for all pairs. The authors prove a Brooks-type theorem: for $k\ge3$, a $k$-connected graph with maximal local edge-connectivity $k$ is $k$-colourable unless it is a complete graph or an odd wheel, which gives a polynomial-time $k$-colouring algorithm for that class. For $k=3$ the two $3$-connected classes coincide, and a $3$-connected graph with maximal local connectivity $3$ is $3$-colourable iff it is not an odd wheel, but for $k=4$ they differ, so the case of $k$-connected graphs with maximal local connectivity $k$, $k\ge4$, remains open. In contrast, $k$-colourability is NP-complete for minimally $k$-connected graphs ($k\ge3$), and $3$-colourability is NP-complete for $(k-1)$-connected graphs with maximal local connectivity $k$.
paper_title: Colouring graphs with constraints on connectivity

title: Conjecture 1.8
statement_text: For fixed $k \geq 4$, there is a polynomial-time algorithm that, given a graph $G$ with maximal local edge-connectivity $k$, finds a $k$-colouring of $G$, or determines that none exists.
context_text: The paper shows that 3-colourability is NP-complete for graphs in $\hat{\mathcal{C}}^k_1$ when $k \geq 4$, so computing the chromatic number or 3-colouring is NP-hard in this class; however, the complexity of $k$-colouring itself for graphs with maximal local edge-connectivity $k$ is unresolved, motivating this conjecture.
notes: The paper remarks that Stiebitz and Toft have recently announced a resolution of this conjecture in the affirmative [24].
paper_title: Colouring graphs with constraints on connectivity
